note.explanation: Computing affects how people work, communicate, trade, and share culture. It brings benefits such as easier communication and new jobs, but it can also create problems such as cyberbullying, misinformation, and reduced privacy. Use technology thoughtfully: check information before sharing it, respect other people’s work, and balance security with ease of use.
examples: A video call lets people communicate across long distances.
A false health story shared on social media can mislead people.
note.checkAnswer: Verify information with reliable sources before believing or sharing it.
note.simple: Computers make many things easier, but people need to use them carefully so the benefits do not cause harm.
note.checkQuestion: What should you do before believing or sharing a story you see on social media?
note.title: How Computing Affects Society
steps: Identify the area affected, such as communication, trade, culture, jobs, or privacy.
State one benefit or change computing brings to that area.
Mention a related risk or trade-off if the question asks for one.
Give a clear example and explain its effect.
note.answer: Computing has benefits, such as instant communication, and risks, such as misinformation. Check information using reliable sources before sharing it.

options: It lets businesses manage transactions and shipments efficiently.
It prevents people from buying products from other countries.
It removes the need to track inventory.
It makes international communication impossible.
mcqs.stem: How do computing systems support global trade?
rationales: This is correct because the section says computers help businesses manage transactions, inventory, and shipments.
This is wrong because online platforms make it easier to buy and sell products around the world.
This is wrong because computers help businesses manage inventory rather than remove its need.
This is wrong because computing enables instant communication across long distances.

options: It can help cultures share traditions and ideas.
It ensures that cultures never change.
It stops people from learning about other cultures.
It only allows local communication.
mcqs.stem: What is one way computing can influence cultural evolution?
rationales: This is correct because online platforms let people share traditions and ideas across cultures.
This is wrong because sharing cultures does not ensure that cultures remain unchanged.
This is wrong because computing can help people learn about cultures through shared content.
This is wrong because computing supports communication across long distances and around the world.

options: It can help people stay connected, but it may also enable cyberbullying.
It makes all online information accurate.
It prevents people from communicating with family.
It has no effect on how people interact.
mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes a social effect of social media?
rationales: This is correct because social media connects people but can also lead to problems such as cyberbullying.
This is wrong because social media can spread false information.
This is wrong because social media can help people connect with friends and family.
This is wrong because technology changes how people interact.

options: Check whether the information comes from reliable sources.
Share it quickly so others can decide if it is true.
Believe it if it has been posted many times.
Trust it if it causes a strong emotional reaction.
mcqs.stem: What is a sensible response to a surprising claim on social media?
rationales: This is correct because the section advises verifying information from reliable sources before believing or sharing it.
This is wrong because sharing unverified information can spread misinformation.
This is wrong because repeated sharing does not prove that a claim is true.
This is wrong because an emotional reaction is not evidence that information is accurate.

options: More automation can replace some traditional jobs.
Computing has ended the need for skilled workers.
Computing affects only jobs in software development.
Automation always creates the same number of jobs it replaces.
mcqs.stem: What is one possible economic risk of computing advancements?
rationales: This is correct because the section explains that automation can replace some roles.
This is wrong because computing also creates job opportunities and does not remove the need for skilled workers.
This is wrong because computing affects many kinds of work, including traditional jobs.
This is wrong because the section does not say that automation replaces and creates equal numbers of jobs.

options: A stronger login process may improve security but take more time.
A stronger login process always makes a system easier to use.
Usability means that a system has no security measures.
Privacy and usability can never affect each other.
mcqs.stem: Which example shows a trade-off between security and usability?
rationales: This is correct because extra verification can improve security while making login less convenient.
This is wrong because the section says stronger measures can make a system less convenient.
This is wrong because usability concerns ease of use, not the absence of security measures.
This is wrong because the section describes trade-offs between privacy, security, and usability.

options: A false health story may spread and lead people to harmful behavior.
False information always disappears before anyone sees it.
Misinformation only affects businesses, not individuals.
Reliable information is harmful because people may share it.
mcqs.stem: Why can misinformation on social media be harmful?
rationales: This is correct because the section gives a false health story as an example that can lead to harmful behavior.
This is wrong because false information can spread quickly.
This is wrong because misinformation can mislead people and affect their behavior.
This is wrong because the section recommends checking reliable information before sharing.

options: Online shopping platforms can help people buy products from different countries.
Online shopping prevents businesses from processing transactions.
Computing systems make it impossible to track shipments.
Global trade requires buyers and sellers to be in the same place.
mcqs.stem: Which is an example of computing supporting global trade?
rationales: This is correct because online platforms allow people to purchase items from different countries.
This is wrong because computers help businesses process transactions efficiently.
This is wrong because computers help businesses track shipments.
This is wrong because online platforms make cross-border buying and selling easier.

written.text: Q11.12. Why is it important to be careful about what you share on social media?
written.finalAnswer: Careless sharing can expose sensitive personal information and affect your privacy. Use privacy settings and avoid sharing sensitive details publicly.

rubric.why: This explains the main risk of careless sharing.
rubric.description: Explain that sharing can expose personal or sensitive information.
rubric.how: State that publicly shared details can affect privacy.

rubric.why: A suitable precaution completes the answer.
rubric.description: Give a safe sharing practice.
rubric.how: Recommend using privacy settings or not posting sensitive details; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Careless sharing can expose sensitive personal information and affect your privacy.
Use privacy settings and avoid sharing sensitive details publicly.
Answer: Be careful because careless sharing can affect your privacy; use privacy settings and avoid posting sensitive information.

written.text: Q11.14. What is the purpose of privacy laws regarding your personal information?
written.finalAnswer: Privacy laws protect personal information and ensure that companies and organizations handle it responsibly.

rubric.why: Identifying what the laws protect is the central point.
rubric.description: State that privacy laws protect personal information.
rubric.how: Name personal information or personal data as the protected material.

rubric.why: This explains how the laws guide organizations.
rubric.description: Explain that organizations must handle data responsibly and prevent misuse.
rubric.how: Mention responsible handling or preventing misuse; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Privacy laws are rules set by the government to protect our personal information.
They ensure that companies and organizations handle our data responsibly.
Answer: Privacy laws protect personal information and require responsible handling of it.

written.text: Q11.15. How do privacy laws protect you from unauthorized access to your data?
written.finalAnswer: Privacy laws set rules for how organizations handle personal data and help prevent it from being misused or accessed without permission.

rubric.why: The answer needs to explain that laws regulate data handling.
rubric.description: State that privacy laws set rules for handling personal data.
rubric.how: Connect legal rules with the way organizations use or protect data.

rubric.why: This identifies the harm the laws help prevent.
rubric.description: Explain that the rules help prevent misuse or unauthorized access.
rubric.how: Mention unauthorized access, access without permission, or misuse; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Privacy laws set rules for how companies and organizations handle personal information.
These rules help prevent data from being misused or accessed without permission.
Answer: Privacy laws regulate data handling and help protect it from unauthorized access or misuse.

written.text: Q11.17. Why is it important to respect intellectual property rights?
written.finalAnswer: Respecting intellectual property rights recognizes creators’ work, prevents unauthorized use, and supports ethical and legal use of their creations.

rubric.why: Respecting creators and their work is the main ethical reason.
rubric.description: Explain that intellectual property rights protect or recognize creators’ work.
rubric.how: Mention creators, their original work, or their rights.

rubric.why: This connects respect for rights with proper use of creations.
rubric.description: Explain that respect avoids unauthorized use and supports ethical or legal use.
rubric.how: Mention unauthorized use, copyright, or ethical use; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Intellectual property rights protect the creations and ideas of individuals and organizations.
Respecting these rights recognizes creators’ work and helps prevent unauthorized use.
Answer: Respect intellectual property rights to recognize creators and use their work ethically and legally.

written.text: Q11.18. What is software piracy, and why is it harmful?
written.finalAnswer: Software piracy is the illegal copying, distribution, or use of software. It is harmful because it violates creators’ rights and the law.

rubric.why: The definition of software piracy is necessary for the answer.
rubric.description: Define software piracy as illegal copying, distribution, or use of software.
rubric.how: Give at least one of the illegal acts and identify software.

rubric.why: The question also asks why piracy is harmful.
rubric.description: Explain that piracy violates rights or the law.
rubric.how: Connect piracy to harm to creators, rights, or legality; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the illegal copying, distribution, or use of software.
It violates creators’ rights and the law.
Answer: Software piracy is illegal copying, distribution, or use of software, and it violates creators’ rights and the law.

written.text: Q11.19. How can you identify reliable sources when researching online?
written.finalAnswer: Check the author’s credentials and the evidence, and compare the information with multiple reputable sources.

rubric.why: Checking source quality or author expertise helps judge reliability.
rubric.description: Explain one way to assess the author or source.
rubric.how: Mention author credentials or reputable and reliable sources.

rubric.why: Cross-checking or examining evidence helps confirm information.
rubric.description: Explain how to check claims against evidence or other sources.
rubric.how: Mention comparing sources, cross-checking, or examining evidence; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Check the author’s credentials and the evidence provided.
Compare the information with multiple reputable sources.
Answer: Check the author and evidence, and cross-check the information with multiple reputable sources.

written.text: Q11.5. Discuss the different types of intellectual property rights, including copyright, trademarks, and patents.
written.finalAnswer: Copyright protects original works; trademarks distinguish a company’s products or services; patents protect new inventions or processes for a certain period.

rubric.why: Copyright is one of the three rights asked about.
rubric.description: Describe what copyright protects.
rubric.how: Explain that copyright gives creators control over original works such as books, music, movies, or software.

rubric.why: Trademarks have a distinct purpose from copyright and patents.
rubric.description: Describe the function of trademarks.
rubric.how: State that symbols, names, or slogans distinguish products or services.

rubric.why: Patents are another separate type of intellectual property right.
rubric.description: Describe what patents protect.
rubric.how: State that patents protect new inventions or processes.

rubric.why: The final point should state the protection or exclusive rights patents give.
rubric.description: State that a patent gives the inventor exclusive rights for a certain period.
rubric.how: Include exclusive rights to make, use, or sell the invention for a certain period; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Copyright is a legal right that gives creators control over their original works, such as music, books, movies, and software.
Trademarks are symbols, names, or slogans used by companies to distinguish their products or services from others.
Patents protect new inventions or processes.
A patent gives the inventor exclusive rights to make, use, or sell the invention for a certain period.
Answer: Copyright protects original works; trademarks distinguish products or services; patents protect new inventions or processes for a certain period.

written.text: Q11.6. Describe the ethical and legal responsibilities related to intellectual property rights. What are the consequences of violating these rights, such as through software piracy or unauthorized use of copyrighted material?
written.finalAnswer: Users should respect creators’ rights, get permission where required, and give credit to original creators. Software piracy and unauthorized use violate intellectual property rights and may have legal consequences.

rubric.why: Respect for creators’ rights is the central ethical responsibility.
rubric.description: State the responsibility to respect intellectual property rights.
rubric.how: Connect ethical use with respecting creators and their work.

rubric.why: Permission and credit show how users can act responsibly.
rubric.description: Explain a proper way to use another person’s work.
rubric.how: Mention getting permission where required or giving credit to the original creator.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the kinds of violations named in the question.
rubric.description: Describe software piracy or unauthorized use of copyrighted material.
rubric.how: Explain that copying, distributing, or using software without authorization violates rights.

rubric.why: The final point explains why violations matter.
rubric.description: State that violations infringe rights and may have legal consequences.
rubric.how: Connect the violation with infringement of creators’ rights or legal consequences; give the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Users have an ethical responsibility to respect the intellectual property rights of creators.
They should get permission where required and give credit to the original creators.
Software piracy is the illegal copying, distribution, or use of software.
Unauthorized use of copyrighted material violates intellectual property rights and may have legal consequences.
Answer: Respect creators’ rights, get permission where required, and give credit; piracy and unauthorized use violate rights and may have legal consequences.

examTips: This section is most likely to be tested with short-answer questions asking for an impact, benefit, risk, or example.
For a question asking for both a benefit and a risk, state each one clearly; for example, social networking connects people but can also lead to cyberbullying or misinformation.
For trade-off questions, name both sides, such as stronger security and reduced convenience.
Marks are earned by giving the point asked for and a relevant example or effect. Do not write only a general statement such as “computers are useful.”

hints: Think about what may happen when personal details are visible to others.
Mention privacy and give one safe sharing practice.

steps.why: The question asks for both a benefit and a risk, so include one of each.
steps.text: Benefit: Social networking helps people stay connected and share information quickly.

steps.why: A relevant risk shows that the effects of computing are not only positive.
steps.text: Risk: Social media can spread false information.

steps.why: A specific effect makes the risk clear and supports the answer.
steps.text: Effect: Misinformation can mislead people and cause confusion.

steps.why: A practical response follows the section’s advice.

example.question: Give one benefit and one risk of social networking, and state what users should do about misinformation.
example.answer: Social networking helps people stay connected and share information quickly, but it can spread misinformation that misleads people. Verify information from reliable sources before believing or sharing it.

explain.title: Computing changes daily life
explain.body: Your textbook says, “Computing technology has a significant effect on our world. It changes how we live, work, and interact with each other.” This means computing affects more than computers: it changes jobs, communication, trade, and social behaviour.

explain.title: Society, culture, and the economy are affected
explain.body: Your textbook says, “Computing affects many aspects of our lives, from the environment to our cultural practices.” Online platforms can help people share traditions and ideas. Computing also creates industries and jobs, while automation can replace some roles.

explain.title: Trade and communication cross borders
explain.body: Your textbook says, “Computing has transformed how we trade, communicate, and share culture globally:” Online shopping helps people buy products from different countries, while email, messaging, and video calls support instant communication.

explain.title: Social networking has benefits and risks
explain.body: Social networking can help people stay in touch and share information quickly. But, as your textbook says, “While social media is useful, it can also spread false information.” Check claims against reliable sources before sharing them.

explain.title: Security can affect convenience
explain.body: Your textbook says, “Sometimes, protecting privacy can make a system less convenient to use.” Strong passwords and two-factor authentication can improve security, but may take longer to use. Systems should balance protection with ease of use.

mistakes: Listing only benefits or only risks when the question asks you to discuss both.
Treating popularity or repeated sharing as proof that online information is true.
Confusing global trade with communication: trade is buying and selling, while communication is exchanging messages or information.
Saying that strong security measures are always convenient; the section explains that security and usability can involve a trade-off.
Giving an example without explaining its effect on people, jobs, culture, or society.
